tests.title: GET single patch returns the patch object plus the 40-character replaced_sha when a backup exists
given: an owned carry_patch workspace with one patch
a stub recovery hook whose ReadReplacedSHA returns a 40-hex SHA for the patch branch
tests.when: the owner, an admin, a PAT with patches:read and a PAT with only patches:write each send GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/patches/:id
then: every call returns 200
the body carries every existing patchResponse field
replaced_sha equals the stub SHA and has 40 hexadecimal characters
tests.pseudocode: for caller in [owner, admin, pat_read, pat_write]: r = get(path, caller); assert r.status == 200; assert r.json.replaced_sha == SHA; assert re.match('^[0-9a-f]{40}$', r.json.replaced_sha); assert r.json.id == patch.id

tests.title: GET omits replaced_sha when there is no backup, no trunk on disk or no hook registered
given: an owned carry_patch workspace with one patch
tests.when: GET is called (a) with a hook reporting no ref, (b) with a hook reporting the trunk is missing, (c) with no hook registered
then: each call returns 200 with the patch object
the raw JSON body contains no replaced_sha key in any of the three cases
tests.pseudocode: for setup in [no_ref_hook, no_trunk_hook, nil_hook]: r = get(path); assert r.status == 200; assert 'replaced_sha' not in r.json

tests.title: A hook error while reading the backup ref is logged at warn level and does not fail GET
given: a stub hook whose ReadReplacedSHA returns an error
a captured log handler
tests.when: GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/patches/:id is called by the owner
then: the status is 200 with the patch object
no replaced_sha key is present
exactly one warn-level log entry is recorded
tests.pseudocode: r = get(path); assert r.status == 200; assert 'replaced_sha' not in r.json; assert count(logs, level=WARN) == 1

tests.title: GET returns a soft-deleted patch with status deleted
given: a patch with status deleted and a non-empty deleted_at
tests.when: the owner calls GET on that patch id
then: the status is 200
status in the body is "deleted"
tests.pseudocode: r = get(path); assert r.status == 200; assert r.json.status == 'deleted'

tests.title: GET with an unknown patch id answers 404 patch not found
given: an owned workspace with no patch of the requested id
tests.when: the owner calls GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/patches/999999
then: the status is 404
the error message is "patch not found"
tests.pseudocode: r = get('/patches/999999'); assert r.status == 404; assert r.json.error.message == 'patch not found'

tests.title: GET by a caller who is neither owner nor admin answers 404 workspace not found
given: a workspace owned by user A and a patch in it
an authenticated user B who is not an admin
tests.when: user B calls GET on the patch
then: the status is 404
the error message is "workspace not found"
tests.pseudocode: r = get(path, as_user_b); assert r.status == 404; assert r.json.error.message == 'workspace not found'

tests.title: GET by a PAT with neither patches:read nor patches:write answers 403
given: a PAT whose permissions are ["workspaces:read"] only
an owned workspace with a patch
tests.when: the PAT calls GET on the patch
then: the status is 403
tests.pseudocode: r = get(path, pat(['workspaces:read'])); assert r.status == 403

tests.title: No other patch endpoint ever returns replaced_sha
given: a stub hook that always returns a backup SHA
tests.when: for any patch endpoint among list, add, update, remove-adjacent responses, restore and sync, and any patch state, the endpoint is called
then: no patch object in any response body contains a replaced_sha key
tests.pseudocode: for ep in [list, add, update, restore, sync]: body = call(ep, gen_patch_state()); for p in patch_objects(body): assert 'replaced_sha' not in p

tests.title: A completed reset returns the patch object with replaced_sha, rebuild_triggered and rebuild_job_id
given: a stub hook whose RunReset returns action replaced, SHAs, rebuild_triggered true and job id "job-1" and whose ReadReplacedSHA returns a SHA
an eligible active patch
tests.when: an authorised caller POSTs .../patches/:id/reset-to-origin
then: the status is 200
the body has the patch fields, replaced_sha, rebuild_triggered true and rebuild_job_id "job-1"
when the stub reports no job, rebuild_triggered is false and rebuild_job_id is absent
tests.pseudocode: r = post(path); assert r.status == 200; assert r.json.rebuild_triggered == True; assert r.json.rebuild_job_id == 'job-1'; assert r.json.replaced_sha == SHA

tests.title: Reset is refused for a PAT without patches:write (403) and for a non-owner (404) before any git operation
given: a stub hook counting RunReset calls
tests.when: a PAT with only patches:read posts the reset, and a non-owner non-admin posts the reset
then: the PAT receives 403
the non-owner receives 404 with message "workspace not found"
RunReset was called zero times
tests.pseudocode: assert post(path, pat(['patches:read'])).status == 403; r = post(path, other_user); assert r.status == 404; assert r.json.error.message == 'workspace not found'; assert hook.calls == 0

tests.title: Reset on an inactive or non-carry_patch workspace answers the same 400 messages as restore
given: one archived workspace and one standard-mode workspace, each with a patch id
tests.when: the owner posts reset-to-origin to each
then: the archived one returns 400 "workspace is not active"
the standard one returns 400 "workspace is not in carry_patch mode"
the hook is not called
tests.pseudocode: assert post(archived).status == 400 and msg == 'workspace is not active'; assert post(standard).status == 400 and msg == 'workspace is not in carry_patch mode'

tests.title: Reset on a workspace whose clone is not ready answers 409 workspace clone is not ready
given: an active carry_patch workspace with clone_status "cloning"
tests.when: the owner posts reset-to-origin
then: the status is 409
the message is "workspace clone is not ready"
the hook is not called
tests.pseudocode: r = post(path); assert r.status == 409; assert r.json.error.message == 'workspace clone is not ready'; assert hook.calls == 0

tests.title: Reset checks unknown id (404) before the integration-branch rule (400) and never calls the hook for either
given: a workspace with integration branch "main"
a patch whose branch_name is "main"
tests.when: the owner posts reset for an unknown id and then for the patch named like the integration branch
then: the unknown id returns 404 "patch not found"
the integration-branch patch returns 400 "patch branch is the integration branch"
the hook is called zero times
tests.pseudocode: assert (post(unknown).status, msg) == (404, 'patch not found'); assert (post(main_patch).status, msg) == (400, 'patch branch is the integration branch'); assert hook.calls == 0

tests.title: Reset on merged_upstream or deleted patches answers 409 with the status in the message
given: one patch with status merged_upstream and one with status deleted
tests.when: the owner posts reset for each
then: each returns 409
the messages are "patch status merged_upstream cannot be reset" and "patch status deleted cannot be reset"
active, conflict and disabled patches pass this check
tests.pseudocode: for s in ['merged_upstream','deleted']: r = post(patch_with(s)); assert r.status == 409; assert r.json.error.message == f'patch status {s} cannot be reset'

tests.title: Reset on a busy workspace answers 409 workspace_busy and writes no ref; the lock is not taken before the checks
given: a real carrypatch recovery hook with a real trunk and a stub fetch recording calls
wslock held for the slug by another operation
tests.when: the owner posts reset for an eligible patch, and separately posts for an ineligible patch while the lock is held
then: the eligible request returns 409 with error type workspace_busy and message "another operation is running on this workspace; retry later"
the fetch stub was not called and every ref is unchanged
the ineligible request returns its own precondition error rather than workspace_busy
tests.pseudocode: unlock = wslock.TryLock(slug); r = post(path); assert r.status == 409 and r.json.error.type == 'workspace_busy'; assert fetch.calls == 0; assert refs_before == refs_after

tests.title: Reset with no recovery hook registered answers 500 patch reset is not configured
given: the recovery hook is nil
tests.when: the owner posts reset for an eligible patch
then: the status is 500
the message is "patch reset is not configured"
tests.pseudocode: RegisterRecoveryHook(nil); r = post(path); assert r.status == 500; assert r.json.error.message == 'patch reset is not configured'

tests.title: Reset fetches the single branch with resolved origin credentials in both modes, then resolves both tips
given: a real bare fork and real trunk
a stub fetch function recording refspec and credentials
PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE set to hub, then origin
credentials in turn: GIT_PAT, GIT_USERNAME/GIT_PASSWORD, none
tests.when: a reset runs in each mode and for each credential configuration
then: the fetch is called once per reset with refspec +refs/heads/<branch>:refs/remotes/origin/<branch>
credentials follow the order GIT_PAT, then username/password, then none
after the fetch the fork tip is read from refs/remotes/origin/<branch>^{commit} and the local tip from refs/heads/<branch>^{commit}
tests.pseudocode: for mode in ['hub','origin']: for creds in cases: reset(); assert fetch.calls[-1].refspec == '+refs/heads/b:refs/remotes/origin/b'; assert fetch.calls[-1].auth == expected(creds)

tests.title: Credential and fetch failures answer 502, echo no error text and write no ref
given: a real trunk with a local branch and a backup ref
a log capture
a resolver failing with text "secret-token-xyz", and a fetch stub failing with text "dial tcp 10.0.0.1 refused"
tests.when: a reset runs under each failure
then: the credential failure returns 502 "failed to resolve origin credentials"
the fetch failure returns 502 "origin fetch failed" with error type origin_fetch_failed
neither response body contains the underlying error text, but the log does
all refs (heads, remotes, backup) are unchanged
tests.pseudocode: r = reset(cred_fail); assert r.status == 502 and r.msg == 'failed to resolve origin credentials'; r = reset(fetch_fail); assert r.json.error.type == 'origin_fetch_failed'; assert 'dial tcp' not in r.body; assert 'dial tcp' in logs; assert snapshot_refs() == before

tests.title: A branch missing on the fork answers 409 missing_on_origin and writes nothing
given: a real bare fork lacking the patch branch
a real trunk holding the branch and a backup ref
the real single-branch fetch classification
tests.when: a reset runs
then: the status is 409
error type is missing_on_origin
message is "branch does not exist on origin"
every ref is unchanged
tests.pseudocode: r = reset(); assert r.status == 409 and r.json.error.type == 'missing_on_origin'; assert r.msg == 'branch does not exist on origin'; assert snapshot_refs() == before

tests.title: Reset creates a missing local branch and reports none for the same commit, writing no backup
given: a real bare fork with the branch
a real trunk once without the local branch and once with it at the fork tip
an existing backup ref in the trunk
tests.when: a reset runs in each case
then: case missing: refs/heads/<branch> equals the fork tip, action created, 200
case same commit: no ref written, action none, 200
refs/hub/replaced/<branch> is unchanged in both cases
tests.pseudocode: r = reset(no_local); assert r.action == 'created'; assert rev('refs/heads/b') == fork_tip; r = reset(same); assert r.action == 'none'; assert rev(backup) == backup_before

tests.title: A fast-forward reset moves the branch, reports fast_forwarded and leaves the existing backup untouched
given: a real fork whose branch is ahead of the trunk's local branch by two commits
an earlier backup ref pointing at an older discarded commit, and a second case with no backup
tests.when: a reset runs
then: refs/heads/<branch> equals the fork tip
action is fast_forwarded
the backup keeps its previous value, or stays absent when there was none
tests.pseudocode: r = reset(); assert r.action == 'fast_forwarded'; assert rev('refs/heads/b') == fork_tip; assert rev_or_none(backup) == backup_before

tests.title: Diverged and fork-behind resets write the backup first, move the branch and report replaced; a repeat overwrites the backup
given: a real fork and trunk with diverged tips
a second scenario where the fork tip is a strict ancestor of the local tip
tests.when: a reset runs for the diverged case, the local branch is advanced by a hub commit, and a second reset runs; then the fork-behind scenario runs
then: after the first reset backup equals the pre-reset local tip, the branch equals the fork tip, action replaced, replaced_sha in the response equals the backup
after the second reset the backup equals the newer local tip
the fork-behind scenario also reports replaced with the old local tip as backup
tests.pseudocode: r1 = reset(); assert r1.action == 'replaced' and rev(backup) == local_before; commit_on_local(); r2 = reset(); assert rev(backup) == local_before2 != local_before

tests.title: Every branch move uses compare-and-swap update-ref and the working tree follows a checked-out branch
given: a real trunk and bare fork
a git runner wrapper recording every command
tests.when: for any random local and fork commit graphs (missing, equal, fast-forward, diverged, behind) and any choice of whether the patch branch is the trunk's checked-out branch, a reset runs
then: the branch write is `update-ref <ref> <new> <expected-old>` and no checkout, reset or branch -f command touches the patch branch
when the branch is checked out, HEAD, index and working tree equal the fork tip afterwards, with no dirty state
the branch ref equals the fork tip when the action is not none
tests.pseudocode: for g in gen_graphs(): setup(g); reset(); assert not any(c.args[0] in ('checkout','branch') for c in runner.cmds); if checked_out: assert git('status --porcelain') == '' and worktree_matches(fork_tip)

tests.title: A lost compare-and-swap race answers 409 ref_changed and any other write failure answers 500, keeping the backup
given: a real trunk and fork with diverged tips
a hook point that makes a hub push move the local branch between SHA resolution and the write
a second scenario where update-ref fails for another reason (read-only ref lock)
tests.when: the reset runs in each scenario
then: the race returns 409 error type ref_changed and message "patch branch changed during reset; retry"
the backup written before the failed move stays and points at the tip read before the race
the other failure returns 500 "failed to update patch branch <branch>"
no further ref writes happen after the failure
tests.pseudocode: r = reset(with_race); assert r.status == 409 and r.json.error.type == 'ref_changed'; assert rev(backup) == tip_read; r = reset(other_fail); assert r.status == 500 and r.msg == 'failed to update patch branch b'

tests.title: In origin mode every completed reset records in_sync state with the fork tip and the current time
given: PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE=origin
a real PatchStore on a test database
a patch with origin_sync_state diverged
reset scenarios for created, none, fast_forwarded and replaced
tests.when: each reset completes
then: the patch row has origin_sync_state in_sync
origin_sha equals the fork tip
origin_synced_at is within a few seconds of now
tests.pseudocode: for action in actions: setup(action); reset(); row = store.get(patch); assert row.origin_sync_state == 'in_sync'; assert row.origin_sha == fork_tip; assert now - row.origin_synced_at < 5s

tests.title: In hub mode a reset writes no origin sync state
given: PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE=hub
a patch row with null origin_* columns and a recording PatchStore
tests.when: a replaced reset completes
then: the origin-state PatchStore method is never called
origin_sync_state, origin_sha and origin_synced_at are unchanged
tests.pseudocode: reset(); assert store.origin_state_calls == 0; assert row_after == row_before

tests.title: A moved active or conflict patch enqueues a rebuild submitted by the caller
given: a real job queue
a patch with status active, then one with conflict
AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC unset
resets with action created, fast_forwarded and replaced
tests.when: each reset completes
then: one rebuild job is enqueued with key slug, group slug:integration_branch and the payload from BuildRebuildPayload
SubmittedBy equals the caller
the response has rebuild_triggered true and rebuild_job_id equal to the job id
tests.pseudocode: r = reset(); job = queue.get(r.rebuild_job_id); assert job.type == 'rebuild' and job.key == slug and job.group == f'{slug}:{integration}'; assert job.submitted_by == caller; assert r.rebuild_triggered

tests.title: AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC=false suppresses the rebuild after a branch move
given: variable AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC set to "false"
an active patch whose reset will replace the branch
tests.when: the reset runs
then: the branch moves
no job is in the queue
response rebuild_triggered is false and has no rebuild_job_id
tests.pseudocode: r = reset(); assert r.rebuild_triggered == False; assert 'rebuild_job_id' not in r; assert queue.count() == 0

tests.title: A moved disabled patch triggers no rebuild
given: a disabled patch whose branch differs from the fork tip
tests.when: the reset runs
then: the branch moves to the fork tip
no job is enqueued
rebuild_triggered is false with no rebuild_job_id
tests.pseudocode: r = reset(disabled_patch); assert rev(branch) == fork_tip; assert queue.count() == 0; assert not r.rebuild_triggered

tests.title: A reset with action none enqueues no rebuild
given: local and fork tips identical
an active patch
tests.when: the reset runs
then: the status is 200
rebuild_triggered is false
no job is enqueued
tests.pseudocode: r = reset(); assert r.status == 200 and r.action == 'none'; assert not r.rebuild_triggered; assert queue.count() == 0

tests.title: A deduplicated rebuild enqueue leaves rebuild_triggered false
given: an already queued rebuild job with the same key and group
an active patch whose branch will move
tests.when: the reset runs
then: the status is 200
rebuild_triggered is false and rebuild_job_id is absent
the queue still holds one job
tests.pseudocode: enqueue_rebuild(slug); r = reset(); assert r.status == 200 and not r.rebuild_triggered; assert 'rebuild_job_id' not in r; assert queue.count() == 1

tests.title: A rebuild enqueue error is logged and the reset still completes
given: a job queue stub whose Enqueue returns an error
an active patch whose branch will move
tests.when: the reset runs
then: the status is 200 with rebuild_triggered false
the branch has moved to the fork tip
an error is logged
tests.pseudocode: r = reset(queue=failing); assert r.status == 200 and not r.rebuild_triggered; assert rev(branch) == fork_tip; assert logs.contains(ERROR_OR_WARN)

tests.title: afc patch reset-to-origin posts to the endpoint with no body and prints the JSON result
given: a stub HTTP server answering 200 with a patch JSON including replaced_sha
tests.when: the command runs with args <slug> <patch-id>
then: the stub received POST /api/v1/workspaces/<slug>/patches/<id>/reset-to-origin
the request body was empty
the exit code is 0 and stdout holds the response JSON
tests.pseudocode: out, code = run(['patch','reset-to-origin','ws','7']); assert stub.method == 'POST' and stub.path == '/api/v1/workspaces/ws/patches/7/reset-to-origin'; assert stub.body == ''; assert code == 0; assert json(out) == response

tests.title: The command rejects any argument count other than two and sends no request
given: a stub HTTP server counting requests
tests.when: the command runs with zero, one and three positional arguments
then: each invocation returns a non-zero exit code
the stub received zero requests
tests.pseudocode: for args in [[], ['ws'], ['ws','1','x']]: code = run(['patch','reset-to-origin']+args); assert code != 0; assert stub.requests == 0

tests.title: A server error status propagates through CLIHandleError with a non-zero exit
given: a stub server answering 409 with message "patch status deleted cannot be reset"
a second stub answering 502 origin fetch failed
tests.when: the command runs against each stub
then: the exit code is non-zero
the server message is reported on the error output
the command has SilenceErrors and SilenceUsage set, so no usage text is printed
tests.pseudocode: out, err, code = run(...); assert code != 0; assert 'cannot be reset' in err; assert 'Usage:' not in err+out; assert cmd.SilenceErrors and cmd.SilenceUsage

tests.title: Help text names the backup ref and replaced_sha and the command defines no flags
given: the constructed PatchCmd tree
tests.when: the reset-to-origin subcommand is found and its help is rendered
then: help contains "refs/hub/replaced/" and "replaced_sha"
the command defines no local flags and no --force flag
tests.pseudocode: c = find(PatchCmd, 'reset-to-origin'); h = help(c); assert 'refs/hub/replaced/' in h and 'replaced_sha' in h; assert c.LocalFlags().lookup('force') is None; assert count(c.LocalNonPersistentFlags()) == 0

tests.title: A real git push that creates, updates or deletes refs/hub/replaced/ is rejected with the fixed message and keeps the old value
given: a running git server over a real trunk with a git:write credential
a pre-receive hook registered that would accept everything
an existing refs/hub/replaced/feature ref
tests.when: a client runs git push for a create of refs/hub/replaced/new, an update of refs/hub/replaced/feature and a delete of refs/hub/replaced/feature
then: each push shows unpack ok and `ng <ref> refs/hub/replaced/ is maintained by the hub and cannot be pushed to`
the registered hook was never consulted for these refs
the trunk's refs/hub/replaced/feature keeps its old value and refs/hub/replaced/new does not exist
tests.pseudocode: out = git_push('+X:refs/hub/replaced/new'); assert 'ng refs/hub/replaced/new refs/hub/replaced/ is maintained by the hub and cannot be pushed to' in out; assert hook.calls == 0; assert rev(trunk, backup) == before

tests.title: Any ref under refs/hub/replaced/ is rejected for any workspace mode, credential and hook state
given: git servers over workspaces in standard and carry_patch modes
with and without a registered pre-receive hook
admin, api key and PAT credentials holding git:write
tests.when: for any ref name starting with refs/hub/replaced/ (including nested and unusual names) and any of those combinations, a client pushes a create, update or delete
then: the ref is rejected with the protected-namespace message
the trunk ref is unchanged
tests.pseudocode: for mode, hook, cred, name, op in product(modes, hooks, creds, gen_names('refs/hub/replaced/'), ops): out = push(op, name); assert rejected(out, name); assert trunk_ref(name) == before

tests.title: A push mixing a protected ref and a normal branch writes the branch and rejects only the protected ref
given: a running git server over a real trunk
an existing backup ref
tests.when: one git push carries refs/hub/replaced/feature and refs/heads/newbranch
then: unpack ok is reported with one ng line for the protected ref and one ok for refs/heads/newbranch
refs/heads/newbranch exists in the trunk at the pushed commit
refs/hub/replaced/feature keeps its old value
tests.pseudocode: out = push(['X:refs/hub/replaced/feature','X:refs/heads/newbranch']); assert 'ok refs/heads/newbranch' in out and 'ng refs/hub/replaced/feature' in out; assert rev(trunk,'refs/heads/newbranch') == X; assert rev(trunk, backup) == before

tests.title: A rejected protected ref triggers no head_sha update, audit entry or post-push hook
given: a git server wired with a recording head_sha updater, audit emitter and post-push hook
a push containing only a protected ref
tests.when: the push is rejected
then: head_sha is unchanged
no audit entry is emitted
the post-push hook is not called
tests.pseudocode: push('X:refs/hub/replaced/f'); assert head_sha_updates == 0; assert audit.events == []; assert post_push.calls == 0

tests.title: Ref names outside refs/hub/replaced/ are never rejected by the protected-namespace rule
given: a git server over a real trunk with no pre-receive hook registered
tests.when: for any ref name outside the prefix, including refs/hub/forward/x, refs/hub/replaced (no trailing slash), refs/hub/replacedx, refs/heads/hub/replaced/x and arbitrary branch names, a client pushes a create
then: the ref is accepted and written
the protected-namespace message never appears
tests.pseudocode: for name in gen_names_not_prefixed('refs/hub/replaced/'): out = push('X:'+name); assert 'ok '+name in out; assert 'maintained by the hub' not in out

tests.title: ls-remote lists the backup ref and a client can fetch it by name
given: a running git server over a trunk holding refs/hub/replaced/feature at a commit not reachable from any branch
tests.when: a client runs git ls-remote and git fetch <hub_url> refs/hub/replaced/feature
then: ls-remote output includes refs/hub/replaced/feature with the backup SHA
the fetch succeeds and the client obtains the backup commit
tests.pseudocode: assert (SHA+'\trefs/hub/replaced/feature') in git('ls-remote', url); git('fetch', url, 'refs/hub/replaced/feature'); assert git('rev-parse FETCH_HEAD') == SHA

tests.title: Hub-internal writes to refs/hub/replaced/ are unaffected by the git server rule
given: a real trunk served by the git server
a hub-internal update-ref and a reset that writes a backup
tests.when: the backup ref is written by update-ref, overwritten, then deleted by the recovery hook

a client fetch sees the value after each write

tests.title: Removing a patch deletes its backup ref and answers 204
given: a real trunk holding refs/hub/replaced/<branch>

the patch row for that branch
tests.when: the owner sends DELETE /workspaces/:slug/patches/:id

the patch row is gone
refs/hub/replaced/<branch> no longer exists
the hook used the branch name from the pre-deletion lookup

tests.title: Removal with no backup ref is a silent success
given: a real trunk without refs/hub/replaced/<branch>

a log capture
tests.when: the patch is removed
then: the status is 204
no warn-level log entry is recorded

tests.title: Removal in a workspace whose trunk is missing succeeds with one info log

a log capture
tests.when: a patch of that workspace is removed
then: the status is 204
one info-level log entry notes the missing trunk
no warn-level entry is recorded
tests.pseudocode: r = delete(path); assert r.status == 204; assert count(logs, INFO, contains='trunk') == 1; assert count(logs, WARN) == 0

tests.title: A hook failure on removal logs a warn entry with slug, branch and error and still answers 204
given: a stub hook whose RemoveBackup returns an error
a log capture
tests.when: the patch is removed
then: the status is 204
the row is deleted
a warn entry carries slug, branch and the error

tests.title: Removal during a running sync does not take the workspace lock and answers 204
given: wslock held for the slug by a simulated sync
a backup ref in the trunk

then: the status is 204, never 409
the backup ref is deleted
the lock remained held by the sync until released by the test

tests.title: Removal with no recovery hook registered works as before
given: the recovery hook is nil
a trunk holding a backup ref
tests.when: the patch is removed
then: the status is 204
the row is deleted
the backup ref is untouched

tests.title: Soft deletion by a rebuild and a later restore keep the backup ref intact
given: a patch with a backup ref pointing at SHA S
a real SQLPatchStore
tests.when: SoftDeletePatch runs, then POST .../restore is called
then: the backup ref equals S after the soft deletion
the backup ref equals S after the restore
